title: Edge-case behavior PRD: chaos readiness and launch checklist for hosted endpoints
creator: Ava Martinez
description: This PRD defines acceptance criteria, test plans, and a launch checklist focused on edge-case behavior and chaos readiness for Redwood hosted endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). The goal is to ensure predictable failure modes, clear degrade paths, and automated validation prior to GA. The document covers requirements for deterministic fallbacks, latency tail mitigation, degraded-feature signaling, data integrity under partial failures, and runbook updates for on-call teams.
background: Customers integrate hosted endpoints into user-facing flows where rare edge cases (KV cache corruption, truncated streaming, partial model timeouts, cross-region failovers) can cause user-visible regressions. Previous launches surfaced gaps: unclear rollback criteria, inconsistent error payloads, and insufficient chaos tests covering mixed-model fallbacks. This PRD narrows scope to behavior contracts and operational readiness checks specifically for hosted endpoints and upgrade paths.
goals: 1) Define behavioral contracts for each endpoint type under partial failure. 2) Establish automated chaos test suites that run in CI and pre-release environments. 3) Provide an exhaustive launch checklist covering telemetry, runbooks, and rollback gates. 4) Ensure clear customer-facing error semantics and metrics for detection and SLO mapping.
non_goals: 1) Model architecture changes. 2) Large refactors of the serving runtime. 3) New billing models or pricing changes. 4) Private deployment offline upgrades (this PRD targets hosted only).
success_metrics: Production error classification coverage >= 95% for edge-case types (timeout, partial-response, kv-miss) within 30 days of launch
Mean time to detect (MTTD) for edge-case regressions < 2 minutes via alerts
Mean time to mitigate (MTTM) for degradations < 15 minutes with documented runbooks
No customer-facing regressions exceeding low-severity SLA breaches in first 30 days across top 10 customers
scope_changes: Initial draft allowed broad chaos testing; scope narrowed to hosted endpoints and to faults that can be simulated in staging without customer data exposure
Request from Support to include more verbose client-facing error codes postponed to follow-up (see PM-715002)
Reduced scope for embedded token-level refunds; finance-led decision to treat refunds as separate billing initiative
requirements: Endpoint behavior contract: every endpoint must return a documented error code namespace for partial results, hard timeouts, and degraded-mode responses
Streaming contract: when streaming is interrupted by server-side preemption, the partial stream must end with a well-formed JSON sentinel and status=partial in metadata
Fallbacks: automatic graded fallback to compatible model variant (e.g., quantized or regional replica) when latency > 99th percentile threshold for 30s, with attribution in telemetry
KV cache integrity: runtime must detect and recover or invalidate KV cache items if checksum mismatch is observed; detection events must be tagged with model and host
Atomic embedding writes: embedding responses stored for cache/replication must be idempotent or deduplicated to prevent duplicated downstream signals
Rerank durability: if rerank step fails during multi-step pipeline, the system must surface the failure and optionally return original un-reranked candidate list with a flag
Operational telemetry: add edge-case-specific dashboards (edge-error-rate, partial-response-rate, fallback-rate) and create alert rules mapped to runbooks

Chaos suites: implement targeted chaos tests that inject the following faults in staging: short process OOMs, KV cache corruption, simulated network partition to regional replica, and delayed kernel operations
API contract: update OpenAPI/SDK docs to include new error codes and degraded-mode semantics
Localization: error messages and sentinel metadata must be stable across regions (no region-specific opaque codes)
Rollout gating: require canary exposure to >= 10% of internal production traffic for 48 hours with no new high-severity customer incidents
api_contract: All endpoints add response field 'behavioral_status' with enum {ok, partial, degraded, error}
When behavior is partial or degraded include 'behavioral_reason' string and optional 'mitigation' object explaining fallback used
Streaming termination rule: final SSE chunk must include 'behavioral_status' and 'sequence_end' fields
Rate-limit responses must continue to return existing rate-limit headers plus behavioral_status=error
acceptance_criteria: Unit and integration tests cover at least five representative edge-case scenarios per endpoint type
End-to-end chaos suite runs in staging and reproduces each documented behavior at least once in CI run
Dashboards for edge-error-rate, fallback-rate, and partial-response-rate exist and have alerting thresholds configured
Runbooks authored and reviewed by SRE and on-call (runbooks include steps to diagnose, mitigate, rollback, and customer-communication templates)
SDKs (Python and Node) return typed errors for new error codes and include documentation snippets
Canary rollout passes the gating criteria: 48 hours at 10% internal traffic, no P0/P1 incidents attributable to new behavioral paths
Documentation (OpenAPI, Console docs, changelog) merged and linked from release notes
Postmortem template and sampling plan created for catching any edge-case incidents in first 30 days
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Merge feature flags and server-side contracts behind 'behavioral_contract_v1' flag in staging
Stage 1: Run automated chaos suite daily in staging for 7 days; collect and triage failures
Stage 2: Internal canary: enable flag for 10% of internal traffic; SRE to observe for 48 hours
Stage 3: Gradual customer canary: 1% -> 5% -> 20% over three 24h windows if no critical alerts
Stage 4: Full rollout with monitoring baseline check and kill-switch available via console
Rollback plan: immediate flag revert + rapid redeploy of previous stable image; customer communication templates prepared
launch_checklist: Telemetry: edge dashboards created and reviewed by Product and SRE
Alerts: thresholds set and on-call escalation path verified
Runbooks: diagnostics and mitigation runbooks published and linked in PagerDuty incidents
Docs: API contract updated, SDK changes published in release notes, and Console warnings added for degraded modes
Chaos tests: green in last 3 CI runs for staging and pre-prod
Security: brief review completed confirming no new PII exposure in error payloads
Legal/Compliance: confirmation that behavior contracts do not change data residency guarantees
Support: Support playbook and customer-facing templates reviewed and staged in the knowledge base
Canary: canary traffic configured and monitoring checklists assigned to owners
Rollback: kill-switch validated by SRE with one-click action and documented expected recovery time
risks: Overly verbose error payloads could leak internal state (mitigation: security review and sanitized fields)
Fallback activation could alter output quality unexpectedly (mitigation: A/B test quality metrics and include fallback attribution)
Chaos tests in staging might not match production failure modes exactly (mitigation: augment with controlled runbook-driven chaos in low-traffic prod windows)
On-call fatigue if noisy alerts are misconfigured (mitigation: conservative thresholds and initial manual paging)
SDK adoption lag: customers using older SDKs may not observe new behavioral_status leading to confusion (mitigation: backwards-compatible defaults and deprecation schedule)
open_questions: Should behavioral_status be exposed in logs by default or behind a debug flag? (proposal: include in telemetry always, expose in API responses by default)
What is the owner for translating behavioral_reason into localized human-readable messages? (proposal: Docs + UX to own customer-facing wording)
Do we need a machine-readable fallback score for downstream ranking decisions? (follow-up to ENG-43900)
Should canary windows for high-SLA customers be extended beyond 48 hours? (suggestion: opt-in extended canary for top 10 customers)
Are there regulatory regions where returning partial results to the client is disallowed? (legal to confirm by 2025-03-07)
How will billing contracts reflect partial responses if payload tokens are trimmed by a degraded path? (finance to advise)
Do we need an audit trail for every fallback activation event for compliance? (security to advise)
Which internal teams need immediate read access to behavioral telemetry? (proposal: SRE, Product, Support lead)
notes_and_links: Related PM: PM-58277 and PM-710002 (error-code standardization)
